newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crudes ease slightly, grades quiet late.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crudes ease slightly, grades quiet late.

text.p: U.S. crudes eased slightly late Tuesday without giving up the bulk of the day's rally that was fueled mainly by strong gasoline prices.
Gasoline climbed on a strike by workers at three refineries belonging to French oil giant Elf Aquitaine, and an explosion at a Texas methanol unit of Hoechst Celanese Corp, traders said.
January West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was trading at $24.75-85, down 15-20 cents from early this afternoon, but up 10 cents from late Monday.
The Jan/Feb WTI spread was steady at around 50 cents.
WTI Jan Posting Plus at Cushing continued to climb, changing hands at $2.34/2.35/2.36/2.37 a barrel.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James was steady at WTI plus 90-93 cts, down about five cts from Monday, although a deal was heard done at a premium of just 89 cents.
West Texas Sour/Midland was heard traded at WTI minus $1.90 a barrel, down about 10 cents from late Monday.
Weak fundamentals continue to plague sour grades.
The weekly report from the American Petroleum Institute (API) indicated a bearish stock build in both gasoline and distillates, while crude showed a minor draw of 868,000 barrels.
This is the fourth consecutive week of crude stock draws.
